sentences.text: Inbound pallets enter the conveyor area only after the preceding inspection and identification steps are complete.
The East Transfer Conveyor carries pallets along the eastern approach to the transfer area.
The West Transfer Conveyor carries pallets along the western approach to the transfer area.
The Conveyor Line Controller sequences pallet movement across the available conveyor sections.
It uses conveyor status and transfer-point signals to determine when a pallet can advance.
The Conveyor Line Controller maintains a separate sequence for each active conveyor path.
Conveyor Line Controller is also known as Brasshaven in local operating terminology.
At each transfer point, interlocks prevent movement into a section that is occupied or unavailable.
Presence sensors confirm that a pallet has reached the expected position before a transfer is initiated.
A blocked transfer point holds the affected pallet upstream while other clear paths may continue operating.
Accumulation zones provide controlled spacing between pallets when downstream movement pauses.
Release from an accumulation zone occurs only when the next conveyor section reports ready.
At a merge, the controller grants passage to one approaching pallet at a time.
The Conveyor Line Controller produces the Transfer Induction Ticket for each accepted induction.
Each output record carries the identifiers and routing details needed to associate the induction with its pallet.
The controller checks that required induction fields are present before releasing the pallet from the transfer point.
Duplicate induction requests are held for resolution rather than treated as new pallet movements.
The North Aisle Stacker Crane sends the Aisle Occupancy Snapshot.
The reported aisle condition reflects the crane's current view of occupied and available storage positions.
Changes in reported conditions support safer decisions about whether an induction can proceed.
The North Aisle Stacker Crane updates its reported condition as its operating state changes.
If reporting becomes stale, the affected induction path remains held until current status is available.
The Warehouse Operations Supervisor can review persistent holds through established operational procedures.
After a fault is cleared, the controller verifies transfer-point readiness before resuming the held sequence.
Normal sequencing resumes without changing the order of pallets already committed to a transfer path.
